Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 168:

God Most High says: ﴿Those who said of their brothers﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: It was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy. Regarding "their brothers" there are two opinions.

The first: they are their brothers in hypocrisy (nifaq). This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas.

(p-499) The second: they are their brothers by lineage (nasab). This is the view of Muqatil. According to the first view, the meaning is: they said to their hypocrite brothers, "If those who were killed with Muhammad had obeyed us, they would not have been killed." According to the second view, the meaning is: they said about their brothers who were martyred at Uhud, "If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed."

God Most High says: ﴿And sat back﴾, meaning the speakers sat back from jihad.

God Most High says: ﴿Then avert from yourselves death, if you are truthful﴾, meaning: Then repel death from yourselves, [the point being] that caution does not avail against decree.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 169:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not think of those who have been killed in the cause of Allah as dead﴾. Ibn 'Amir recited "quttilu" (qutilū) with the doubled letter (tashdid). The scholars differed regarding who this verse was revealed about, in three opinions.

The first: it was revealed concerning the martyrs of Uhud. Ibn 'Abbas narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "When your brothers were struck at Uhud, Allah placed their souls in the crops of green birds, which come to the rivers of Paradise, eat from its fruits, and take shelter in golden lamps suspended in the shade of the Throne. When they found the goodness of their food and drink and the beauty of their resting place, they said: 'Would that our brothers knew what Allah has done for us, so that they would not lose interest in jihad and would not shrink from war.' Allah, exalted is He, said: 'I will convey it on your behalf.' So Allah revealed this verse." This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Abu al-Duha.

The second: it was revealed concerning the martyrs of Badr, when they attained the honour of Allah, exalted is He, and said: "Our Lord, would that our brothers knew," so this verse and the one following it were revealed. Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas, and it is the view of Muqatil.

The third: it was revealed concerning the martyrs of Bi'r Ma'una. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from some of his shaykhs that the Prophet (ﷺ) sent al-Mundhir ibn 'Amr with seventy men from the best of the Muslims to the people of Najd. When they reached Bi'r Ma'una, Haram ibn Milhan went out to 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl with the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but 'Amir did not even look at it, and a man from behind the house came out with a spear and struck Haram in the side until it came out the other side. He said: "Allahu Akbar! I have succeeded, by the Lord of the Ka'ba!" The rest of his companions were also killed, except for some of them. Anas ibn Malik said: "Allah revealed concerning them: 'Convey to our people on our behalf that we have met our Lord, and He is pleased with us and we are pleased with Him,' and then it was abrogated (rufi'at), and this verse was revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who have been killed in the cause of Allah as dead﴾."

This is the difference among the people regarding who it was revealed about. They also differed regarding the occasion of its revelation, in three opinions.

The first: after their martyrdom, the martyrs asked Allah to inform their brothers of their fate; this has been mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: a man said: "Would that we knew what our brothers who were martyred have encountered," and so it was revealed; this was said by Muqatil.

The third: when the relatives of the martyrs experienced blessing or joy, they would grieve and say: "We are in blessing and joy while our fathers, our sons, and our brothers are in the graves." So this verse was revealed. 'Ali ibn Ahmad al-Nisaburi mentioned it.

As for the interpretation, the meaning of the verse is: do not think of them as dead like the dead who were not killed in the cause of Allah. We have explained this meaning in (al-Baqara), and we mentioned that the meaning of their life is that their souls are in the crops of birds that eat from the fruits of Paradise and drink from its rivers. Mujahid said: "They are provided with sustenance from the fruit of Paradise."

(p-502) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Rejoicing﴾. Ibn Qutaybah said: al-farah (joy) is gladness. As for "that which Allah has given them," they attained nothing of Allah's honour and provision. And al-istibshar (rejoicing at good tidings) is gladness at glad tidings. ﴿Concerning those who have not yet joined them from behind them﴾: their brethren among the Muslims. Regarding the cause of their rejoicing over them, there are three opinions.

The first: when Allah, Exalted, informed them of the honour of the martyrs, He informed the martyrs that "I have sent down to your Prophet and informed him of your affair," so they rejoiced and knew that their brethren would be eager for martyrdom. This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The second: they rejoice over their brethren who hope for martyrdom for them, saying: if they are killed, they will attain what we have attained of virtue. This was said by Qatadah.

The third: the martyr is brought a book containing the mention of those of his brethren and family who preceded him, and in it: "So-and-so will come to you on such-and-such a day," and he rejoices at his arrival, just as the family of an absent person rejoices at him. This is the saying of al-Suddi.

The "ha'" and "mim" in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿No fear shall be upon them﴾ refer to those who have not yet joined them. Al-Farra' said: its meaning is that they rejoice for them, that there is no fear upon them and no grief. Regarding what the "fear" and "grief" are lifted from them, there are two opinions.

One: there is no fear upon them concerning those they left behind of their offspring, nor do they grieve over what they left of their wealth.

The second: there is no fear upon them concerning what they are going to face, and they do not grieve over parting from the world, being joyful in the Hereafter.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They rejoice in a blessing from Allah and a bounty﴾. Muqatil said: "[It means] with mercy and provision."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And that Allah﴾. The majority of reciters read it with a fatha (wa-anna), meaning: "and they rejoice that Allah [does not waste the reward of the believers]." Al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra (wa-inna), as a new sentence (isti'naf).

(p-503) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who responded to God and the Messenger﴾. Concerning the occasion of its revelation there are two accounts.

The first: "When the polytheists turned back on the day of Uhud, the Prophet ﷺ called his companions to pursue them. He then went out with those who responded to his call. He met Abu Sufyan with a group of people, and Abu Sufyan said: 'If you meet Muhammad, inform him that I am gathering a great host.' The Prophet ﷺ met them and asked them about him. They said: 'We met him with a great host, and we see you in a small number.' But he refused except to pursue him, so Abu Sufyan outstripped him and entered Makkah. Then this verse was revealed." This is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas and the majority.

The second: "When Abu Sufyan wished to turn away from Uhud, he said: 'O Muhammad, our appointment between us and you is the season of Badr.' When the following year came, Abu Sufyan set out, but God cast terror into his heart, and he resolved to turn back. He met Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud and said: 'I have arranged with Muhammad and his companions that we meet at the lesser season of Badr, but this is a year of drought, unsuitable for us.' So he (Nu'aym) discouraged them from us, and informed them that we had a great host. He met them and frightened them, and they said: 'God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.' The Prophet ﷺ went out with his companions and they stayed at Badr waiting for Abu Sufyan, and then the saying of God, exalted is He, was revealed: ﴿Those who responded to God and the Messenger﴾, the verses..." This meaning is related from Mujahid and Ikrimah. The word istijabah means ijabah (responding). They recited:

*"So none responded to him at that time with an answer,"*

meaning: so none answered him.

Concerning what was intended by the Prophet ﷺ, his going out, and his calling the people to go out, there are three opinions.

The first: to strike terror into the enemy by pursuing them. The second: for the appointment with Abu Sufyan. The third: because it reached him that the people had said: "You have hit their strength, then you left them." The discussion of the wound has already preceded.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿for those among them who did good﴾, meaning: those who did good by obeying the Messenger and guarded against opposing him.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 173:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those to whom the people said﴾. Regarding who is meant by "the people," there are three opinions.

The first: They were a caravan that Abu Sufyan met, and he guaranteed them a reward in exchange for frightening the Prophet ﷺ and his companions. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Ishaq.

The second: It was Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud al-Ashja'i. This was said by Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, and Muqatil, among others.

(p-505). The third: They were the hypocrites. When they saw the Prophet ﷺ preparing for campaign, they forbade the Muslims from going out and said: "If you go to them in their homes, not one of you will return." This is the saying of al-Suddi.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the people have gathered against you﴾, meaning Abu Sufyan and his companions.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿so it increased them in faith﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: That frightening increased them in steadfastness in their religion and in persistence in supporting their Prophet. And they said: ﴿Sufficient for us is Allah﴾, meaning: He is the One who suffices us in their affair. As for "al-Wakil" (the Trustee/Disposer of affairs), al-Farra' said: al-Wakil means the Sufficient, and Ibn al-Qasim preferred this view. Ibn Qutaybah said: He is the Guarantor (al-Kafil). He said: A man's wakil over his property is the one who has guaranteed it for him and taken charge of it. Al-Khattabi said: al-Wakil is the Guarantor of the sustenance and welfare of the servants, and its true meaning is that He is the One who independently carries out the matter entrusted to Him. Ibn al-Anbari related that some people said: al-Wakil is the Lord.

The commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 174:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So they returned with a favor from Allah﴾. *Al-inqilab* means returning. Regarding the "favor," there are three views.

The first is that it is the reward. This was said by Mujahid. The second is well-being (*al-'afiya*). This was said by al-Suddi.

(p-٥٠٦) The third is faith and victory. This was said by al-Zajjaj. Regarding the "bounty," there are three views.

The first is the profit of trade. This was said by Mujahid and al-Suddi, and this is the view of those who hold that they went out to the appointment with Abu Sufyan. Al-Zuhri said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) called the Muslims to muster for the appointment with Abu Sufyan at Badr, they set out with their merchandise, and they said: 'If we meet Abu Sufyan, then he is the one we went out to. If we do not meet him, we will trade with our goods.' Badr was a market held every year, so they set off, attended to their needs, and Abu Sufyan broke the appointment."

The second is that they came upon a *sariyya* (a raiding detachment) at al-Safra', and were provided with spoils from it. This was said by Muqatil.

The third is that it is the reward. Al-Mawardi mentioned this.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿No harm touched them﴾. Ibn Abbas said: No one harmed them. ﴿And they followed the pleasure of Allah﴾ in pursuing the people. ﴿And Allah is the Owner of great bounty﴾, meaning: Possessor of grace by repelling the polytheists from the believers.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 176:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not let those who hasten into disbelief grieve you﴾. Nafi' read "yahzunaka" and "li-yahzunani" and "li-yuhzina," with a dammah on the yaa' and a kasrah on the zaay, throughout the Qur'an, except in (al-Anbiya') at "la yahzunuhumu al-fazaʿ" [al-Anbiya': 103], where he opened the yaa' and put a dammah on the zaay. The rest read every instance in the Qur'an with a fathah on the yaa' and a dammah on the zaay. Abu 'Ali said: It is likely that Nafi' followed a reported tradition in surah al-Anbiya', or he preferred to take both readings.

Regarding "those who hasten into disbelief" there are four opinions.

One: they are the hypocrites and the leaders of the Jews. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

Two: they are the hypocrites. This was said by Mujahid.

Three: they are the disbelievers of Quraysh. This was said by al-Dahhak.

Four: they are a people who apostatized from Islam. This was mentioned by al-Mawardi.

It was also said: the meaning of their hastening into disbelief is their supporting the disbelievers and their aiding them. If it is asked: how is it that their hastening into disbelief does not grieve him? The answer: their action should not grieve you, for you will be victorious over them.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, they will not harm Allah at all﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions.

One: they will not diminish anything of Allah by their disbelief. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil.

Two: they will not harm the friends of Allah at all. This was said by 'Ata'. Ibn 'Abbas said: "al-hazz" means the portion, and "al-akhirah" means Paradise. ﴿And for them is a great punishment﴾ in the Fire.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who have exchanged disbelief for faith﴾. Mujahid said: "They are the hypocrites (al-munafiqun) who believed and then disbelieved." The meaning of "exchanging" (al-ishtira') has already been discussed in (Al-Baqarah).

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 178:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve suppose that Our giving them respite is good for them themselves﴾. The scholars differed concerning whom it was revealed about, in four opinions.

The first: it concerns the Jews, the Christians and the hypocrites; this was said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: it concerns the Banu Qurayza and the Banu al-Nadir; this was said by Ata.

The third: it concerns the polytheists of Makkah; this was said by Muqatil.

(p-509) The fourth: it concerns every disbeliever; this was said by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi.

Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr and Nafi' recited ﴿Wa la yahsabanna alladhina kafaru﴾ [Al 'Imran: 178], ﴿Wa la yahsabanna alladhina yabkhalun﴾ [Al 'Imran: 180], and ﴿Wa la yahsabanna alladhina yafrahun﴾ [Al 'Imran: 188], with the ya' (yahsabanna, third person) and a kasra on the sin. Ibn Amir agreed with them, except that he put a fatha on the sin. Hamzah recited these with the ta' (tahsabanna, second person). Asim and al-Kisai recited everything in this surah with the ta', except two letters: ﴿Wa la yahsabanna alladhina kafaru﴾ and ﴿Wa la yahsabanna alladhina yabkhalun﴾, which are with the ya'; except that Asim put a fatha on the sin, while al-Kisai put a kasra on it. They did not differ over ﴿Wa la tahsabanna alladhina qutilu﴾ that it is with the ta'.

﴿Wa numli lahum﴾ means: We prolong for them their lifespan. A similar usage is: ﴿wahjurni maliyya﴾. Ibn al-Anbari said: the derivation of "numli lahum" is from al-malwa, which is a period of time. It is said: malwatun min al-dahr, and milwatun, mulwatun, milawatun, mulawatun, and malawatun, with one meaning. From it is their saying: "Wear the new and enjoy the beloved," meaning: so that your days with him may be prolonged.

Mutammim ibn Nuwayra said:

"I wish that I could enjoy his lifespan, with my wealth from the wealth of Tarif and Talid."

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 179:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in﴾. Regarding its occasion of revelation there are five opinions.

(p-510) The first: The Quraysh said: "Do you claim, O Muhammad, that whoever follows you is in Paradise and whoever opposes you is in the Fire?" So He informed us of who believes in you and who does not believe, and this verse was revealed. This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: The believers asked to be given a sign by which they could distinguish the believer from the hypocrite, so this verse was revealed. This is the saying of Abu al-'Aliyah.

The third: "The Prophet ﷺ said: 'I was shown my Ummah, and I was informed of who believes in me and who disbelieves.' This reached the hypocrites, and they mocked and said: 'We are with him, and yet he does not know us.' So this verse was revealed." This is the saying of al-Suddi.

The fourth: The Jews said: "O Muhammad, you were content with our religion. What will become of you if some of you die before your Book is revealed?" So this verse was revealed. This is the saying of 'Umar, the mawla of Ghafrah.

The fifth: A group of hypocrites claimed that their faith was like the faith of the believers, so Allah exposed their hypocrisy on the Day of Uhud, and revealed this verse. This is the saying of Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi.

Regarding those addressed by this verse there are two opinions.

One: They are the disbelievers and the hypocrites. This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak.

The second: They are the believers, and the meaning is: Allah would not leave you in the state you are in, of the mixing of the believer with the hypocrite. Al-Tha'labi said: This is the saying of most of the scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani).

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿until He distinguishes the wicked from the good﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu 'Amr and Ibn 'Amir read "hatta yamiza" and "liyamiza Allahu al-khabitha" with an open yā' and light (unshaddated) mīm. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf and Ya'qub read "yumayyiza" with a shaddah, and likewise in [al-Anfal: 37] (liyumayyiza Allahu al-khabitha).

Abu 'Ali said: "mizta" and "mayyaztu" are two dialects. Ibn Qutaybah said: The meaning of yumayyiz is: yukhallis (separates out). As for al-tayyib, it is the believer. Regarding al-khabith there are two opinions.

One: It is the hypocrite. This was said by Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj.

The second: It is the disbeliever. This was said by Qatadah and al-Suddi. Regarding that by which the distinction between them occurs there are three opinions.

The first: It is emigration and fighting. This was said by Qatadah, and it is the view of those who say al-khabith is the disbeliever.

The second: It is jihad, and this is the view of those who say it is the hypocrite. Mujahid said: So Allah distinguished on the Day of Uhud between the believers and the hypocrites, when they showed their hypocrisy and held back.

The third: It is all the obligations and duties, for the believer's state is hidden by his profession of faith, but when the duties come, his condition becomes clear. This is the saying of Ibn Kaysan.

Regarding those addressed by His saying: ﴿Nor would Allah reveal to you the unseen﴾ there are two opinions.

One: They are the disbelieving Quraysh, so the meaning is: Allah would not make clear to you the believer from the disbeliever, because they had asked for that, saying: "Inform us of who believes and who does not believe." This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: It is the Prophet ﷺ, so the meaning is: Nor would Allah reveal the unseen to Muhammad. This was said by al-Suddi. "Yajtabi" means "yakhtar" (chooses), as said by al-Zajjaj and others. So the meaning of the statement according to the first view is: Allah does not reveal the unseen to anyone except the prophets whom He chooses; and according to the second view: Allah does not reveal the unseen to anyone except that He chooses whom He wills and reveals to him what He wills.

﴿And let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think that it is better for them﴾. They differ over who this verse was revealed about, on two views.

The first: it was revealed about those who refused to pay the zakat (obligatory almsgiving) on their wealth. This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Hurayrah, Ibn 'Abbas in the narration of Abu Salih, al-Sha'bi, Mujahid, and in a narration of al-Suddi, among others.

The second: it was revealed about the rabbis who concealed the description and prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ). This was narrated by 'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas, and by Ibn Jurayj from Mujahid, and al-Zajjaj preferred it.

Al-Farra' said: The meaning of the speech is: "Let not those who are stingy think that stinginess is good for them." He mentioned "yabkhalun" (they withhold) and left out "al-bukhl" (stinginess), as you say: "So-and-so arrived, and I was delighted by him," meaning, "I was delighted by his arrival."

The poet said:

"When the fool is forbidden, he rushes toward it and opposes, and the fool is toward opposition."

He means: he rushes toward foolishness. As for ﴿what Allah has given them﴾, according to the one who said the stinginess is in paying zakat, it is wealth; and according to the one who said the stinginess is in concealing the description of the Prophet (ﷺ), it is knowledge.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Hu﴾ ("it") refers to the stinginess, though it is not mentioned explicitly, but it is indicated by "yabkhalun" (they withhold). Regarding the meaning of "they will be encircled by it," there are four views.

The first: it will be made into something like a serpent that encircles the person. Ibn Mas'ud narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "No man withholds the zakat of his wealth except that on the Day of Resurrection it will be presented to him as a bald, venomous male snake that flees from him, while it pursues him, until it is put around his neck." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿They will be encircled with what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection﴾. This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud and Muqatil.

The second: it will be made into a collar of fire. This was narrated by Mansur from Mujahid and Ibrahim.

The third: the meaning of encircling them with it is that they are charged to bring it, narrated by Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid.

The fourth: its meaning is that its sin will cling to their necks, said by Ibn Qutaybah.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: The people of the heavens and the people of the earth will die, and the Lord of the worlds will remain. Al-Zajjaj said: The people were addressed in terms they understand, because they consider whatever returns to a person as an inheritance when it becomes his property. Ibn al-Anbari said: The meaning of inheritance is (p-٥١٤) that a man is alone with something he was not alone with before. When creation dies and the Mighty and Majestic One remains alone, that becomes His inheritance.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read "ya'malun" (they do) with the "ya" (third person), following His saying ﴿they will be encircled﴾. The rest read it with the "ta" (second person), because before it is ﴿And if you believe and fear Allah﴾.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 181:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich."﴾ Concerning the occasion of its revelation there are two accounts.

One of them: "Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) entered the house of study (midras) of the Jews and found them gathered around a man among them named Finhas. Abu Bakr said: 'Fear Allah and embrace Islam, for by Allah, you know that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'By Allah, O Abu Bakr, we have no need of Allah; rather, it is He who is in need of us. If He were free of need of us, He would not have borrowed from us.' Abu Bakr became angry and struck Finhas's face a severe blow, and said: 'By Allah, were it not for the treaty between us, I would strike off your neck.' Finhas went complaining to the Prophet (ﷺ), and Abu Bakr informed him of what he had said. Finhas denied it. So this verse was revealed, and there was revealed concerning what reached Abu Bakr of anger ﴿And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with Allah much hurt﴾ [Al 'Imran: 186]." This is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas, and to a similar view went Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Suddi, and Muqatil.

The second: when the verse ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 245] was revealed, the Jews said: "Only a poor person borrows from a wealthy one." So this verse was revealed. This is the statement of al-Hasan and Qatadah.

Concerning those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor," there are four views.

(p-515) The first: that he was Finhas ibn 'Azura' the Jew. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil.

The second: Huyayy ibn Akhtab. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah.

The third: that a group of the Jews said it. Mujahid said: Abu Bakr struck a man from among those who said, ﴿Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich﴾, [saying], "He did not borrow from us while He is rich?!"

The fourth: that he was al-Nabbash ibn 'Amr the Jew. Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi mentioned it.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We will record what they have said﴾. Hamzah alone read "sayuktabu" with a dammah on the yaa', and "qatluhum" in the nominative (raf'), and "yaqulu" with a yaa'. The rest read (sanaktubu ma qalu) with a nun, and "qatlahum" in the accusative (nasb), and "naqulu" with a nun. Ibn Mas'ud read "wa-yuqalu", and al-A'mash and Talhah read "wa-yaqulu".

Regarding the meaning of ﴿We will record what they have said﴾ there are two views.

One: "We will preserve for them what they have said," said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: "We will command the angels who record to write it down," said by Muqatil.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and their killing of the prophets﴾, meaning: and We will record that. If it is said: this speaker never killed a prophet, the answer is that he approved of the deed of his predecessors in that, as we explained in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and they kill the prophets without right﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of ﴿the punishment of burning﴾ is a burning punishment, i.e., a punishment by fire, because punishment may be by other than fire.
Allah's saying: ﴿That﴾ refers to the punishment, and ﴿what your hands have sent before﴾ means disbelief and sins.

(p-516) "His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those who say, 'Indeed, Allah has taken a covenant from us'﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: It was revealed concerning Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, Malik ibn al-Sayf, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, and a group of the Jews, who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'Indeed, Allah has taken a covenant from us,' i.e., He commanded us in the Torah: 'that we should not believe in a messenger,' i.e., we should not affirm a messenger who claims to be a messenger, '﻿until he brings us an offering which the fire consumes.'" Ibn Qutaybah said: The qurban (offering) is that which is brought near to Allah the Exalted, such as an animal sacrificed or other things. They only requested the qurban because it was among the practices of the earlier prophets, and the descent of fire was a sign of acceptance. Ibn 'Abbas said: A man would give charity, and if it was accepted from him, a fire would descend from the sky and consume it; it was a fire that had a roaring sound and a crackling. 'Ata' said: The Children of Israel would slaughter for Allah and take the choicest pieces of meat, placing them in the middle of the house beneath the sky. The prophet would stand in the house and commune with his Lord, and a fire would descend and take that offering, and the prophet would fall down prostrate, and Allah would reveal to him whatever He wills. Ibn 'Abbas said: Say, O Muhammad, to the Jews: ﴿Messengers have certainly come to you before me with clear proofs﴾, i.e., with signs, ﴿and with what﴾ you have asked of the offering.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 184:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if they deny you, then indeed messengers before you were denied﴾. Its meaning: you are not the first messenger who was denied.

Abu Ali said: Ibn Amir alone read "bil-bayyinati waz-zuburi" with an added bi' (the preposition "bi"), and likewise it is in the codices of the people of Syria. Its rationale is that repeating the bi' is a form of emphasis. The rationale of the reading of the majority (p-517) is that the waw has already done the work of repeating the governing particle: you say "I passed by Zayd and Amr," and so you dispense with repeating the bi'.

Al-Zajjaj said: "az-Zuburu" is the plural of "zabur," and a zabur is every book containing wisdom.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and the Book that gives light﴾. Abu Sulayman said: he means by it the books that are luminous with proofs and arguments.

The Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on Surah 3, verse 185:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Every soul shall taste death﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "When His saying was revealed, ﴿Say: The Angel of Death who has been charged with you will take you﴾ [al-Sajdah: 11], they said: 'O Messenger of Allah, it was only revealed concerning the children of Adam. Where is the mention of death for the jinn, the birds, and the livestock?' So this verse was revealed." In the mention of death there is a warning to those who deny the return, an encouragement to renounce the world, and an admonition to seize the opportunity of the appointed term.

And in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And you will only be paid your full rewards on the Day of Resurrection﴾, there is good news for the good-doers and a warning for the evildoers.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Whoever is drawn away from the Fire﴾. Ibn Qutaybah said: "Saved and kept far away." ﴿Then he has certainly succeeded﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: "The interpretation of fāza (succeeded) is that he has moved far from what is disliked and has attained what he loves. It is said of one who is saved from destruction, and of one who attains what he is happy with: 'He has succeeded.'"

(p-518) His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the worldly life is not but the enjoyment of delusion﴾. He means that living in it deceives a person with what it promises him of lasting long, while it will soon come to an end. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: "It is the enjoyment of delusion for one who does not busy himself with seeking the Hereafter. As for one who busies himself with seeking the Hereafter, it is for him an enjoyment that conveys him to what is better than it."

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 186:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿You will surely be tested in your possessions and in your persons﴾. Regarding the occasion of its revelation there are five opinions.

The first: "The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by a gathering in which was ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy and ʿAbdullah ibn Rawaha. The dust of the animal covered the gathering, so Ibn Ubayy covered his nose with his cloak and said: 'Do not raise dust over us.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dismounted, then invited them to Allah and recited the Qur'an to them. Ibn Ubayy said: 'There is nothing better than what you say, but if it is true, do not trouble us in our gatherings.' Ibn Rawaha said: 'Bring it to us in our gatherings, O Messenger of Allah, for we love that.' The Muslims, the polytheists and the Jews then began to revile one another, and this verse was revealed." Narrated by ʿUrwa from Usama ibn Zayd.

(p-519) The second: The polytheists and the Jews used to harm the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions with the greatest harm, so this verse was revealed. Said by Kaʿb ibn Malik al-Ansari.

The third: It was revealed concerning what took place between Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Finhas the Jew, and its mention has already preceded from Ibn ʿAbbas.

The fourth: It was revealed concerning the Prophet (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. Said by Abu Salih from Ibn ʿAbbas, and Muqatil chose it. ʿIkrima said: It was revealed concerning the Prophet (ﷺ), Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and Finhas the Jew.

(p-520) The fifth: It was revealed concerning Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, who in his poetry incited the polytheists against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions. This is the view of al-Zuhri.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of "latublawunna" is "latukhtabarunna" (you will surely be tested), i.e., trials will befall you, so that the believer is distinguished from others. The "nun" was added for emphasis together with the oath particle (lam al-qasam), the waw was given a damma because of its sukun, and the nun's sukun (as well) [was retained]. Regarding being tested in possessions there are two opinions.

One: their loss and diminution. The second: the obligatory rights (ḥuqūq) that are imposed upon them.

Regarding being tested in persons there are four opinions.

One: calamities and killing. The second: the obligatory acts of worship imposed.

The third: illnesses. The fourth: calamity through relatives and kin.

ʿAtaʾ said: They are the emigrants, whose possessions the polytheists seized, whose homes they sold, and whom they tortured.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And you will surely hear from those who were given the Book﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: They are the Jews and the Christians, and "those who associated partners" are the polytheists of the Arabs. ﴿And if you are patient﴾ over the harm, ﴿and fear Allah﴾ by abstaining from His disobediences.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, that is of the determined matters﴾, i.e., of what is resolved upon, because of its clear rightness.

Section

The majority hold this verse to be muhkam (not abrogated). Some people held that the patience mentioned here is abrogated by the verse of the sword.

(p-521) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture﴾. Concerning them there are three opinions.

The first: they are the Jews. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, and Muqatil. According to this, "the Scripture" is the Torah.

The second: they are the Jews and the Christians, and "the Scripture" is the Torah and the Gospel.

The third: they are all the scholars, so "the Scripture" is a noun of genus (ism jins).

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You shall make it clear to the people﴾.

Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Abu Bakr, al-Mufaddal from 'Asim, and Zayd from Ya'qub read (liyubayyinunnahu lil-nas wa la yaktumunahu) with the ya' in both places. The rest, and Hafs from 'Asim, read with the ta' in both places. Concerning the pronominal suffix (ha' al-kinaya) in "latubayyinunnahu" and "taktumunahu" there are two opinions.

The first: it refers to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. This is the view of those who said they are the Jews.

The second: it refers to the Scripture. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah, and it is the more correct view, because the Scripture is the nearest of the two mentioned, and because part of making them clear is revealing the description of Muhammad ﷺ in it. This is the view of those who held that it is general to every Scripture. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Allah did not take a covenant from the ignorant that they should learn, until He had taken a covenant from the learned that they should teach.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So they threw it behind their backs﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: that is, they cast it away. It is said of one who discards a thing and pays it no heed: "You have made this matter a thing behind the back." Al-Farazdaq said:

"Tamim ibn Qays, let not my need be cast behind your back, nor let its answer be beyond me."

(p-522) Its meaning: do not let my need be neglected by you, cast aside. Concerning the pronoun in "fanabadhuhu" there are two opinions.

The first: it refers to the covenant. The second: it refers to the Scripture.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they sold it﴾. That is, they exchanged what Allah had taken from them, namely upholding it, and what He had promised them for it, Paradise, ﴿for a small price﴾, that is, a meager gain of the worldly life.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 188:

The words of the Most High: (Let not those who rejoice in what they have brought) — the people of Kufa read: "Do not think" with the ta' (tā'). There are eight opinions concerning the occasion of its revelation.

The first: "The Prophet ﷺ asked the Jews about something, and they concealed it and informed him of something else, and they showed him that they had informed him of it, and they sought praise from him by that, and rejoiced in what they had brought by their concealment of it from him. So this verse was revealed."

(p-523) The second: it was revealed concerning a group of Jews who rejoiced in what they obtained of the world, and loved that people would say they were scholars. This opinion and the one before it are from Ibn ʿAbbas.

The third: the Jews said, "We are upon the religion of Ibrahim," and they concealed the mention of Muhammad ﷺ, so this verse was revealed. Said by Saʿid ibn Jubayr.

The fourth: the Jews of Madina wrote to the Jews of Iraq and Yemen, and to whoever among their scribes among the Jews reached them throughout the earth: "Muhammad is not a prophet, so hold firm to your religion." Their word thus united upon disbelief in him, and they rejoiced in that and said, "We are the people of fasting and prayer, and the friends of Allah," so this verse was revealed. This is the saying of al-Dahhak and al-Suddi.

The fifth: "The Jews of Khaybar came to the Prophet ﷺ and his companions and said, 'We are upon your opinion, and we are a support for you,' while they were holding firmly to their misguidance. They wished that a prophet of Allah would praise them for what they had not done, so this verse was revealed." Said by Qatada.

The sixth: some Jews equipped an army against the Prophet ﷺ and agreed upon it, so this verse was revealed. Said by Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi.

The seventh: "A group of the People of the Book entered upon the Prophet ﷺ, then went out from his presence and told the Muslims that they had been informed of things that they knew, so they praised them, while concealing the opposite of what they displayed, so this verse was revealed." Mentioned by al-Zajjaj.

The eighth: men from among the hypocrites used to remain behind from the expedition with the Prophet ﷺ; when he returned, they apologized to him and swore oaths, and they loved to be praised for what they had not done, so this verse was revealed. Said by Abu Saʿid al-Khudri. (p-524) This opinion indicates that it was revealed concerning the hypocrites, while the sayings before it indicate that it was concerning the Jews.

Concerning "what they had brought," there are eight opinions.

The first: it is their concealment of the truth they knew.

The second: their alteration of the Torah. The third: their preference of the perishing worldly life over the reward.

The fourth: their misleading of the people. The fifth: their gathering together in denying the Prophet.

The sixth: their hypocrisy, by displaying the opposite of what was in their hearts.

The seventh: their agreement to fight the Prophet ﷺ. These are the opinions of those who said they are the Jews.

The eighth: their staying behind in the military expeditions. This is the saying of those who said they are the hypocrites.

Concerning the words of the Most High: ﴿And love to be praised for what they did not do﴾, there are six opinions.

(p-525) The first: they loved to be praised for answering the Prophet ﷺ about something he asked them, when they had not answered him.

The second: they loved that people would say they were scholars, and they were not so.

The third: they loved to be praised for what they had not done of prayer and fasting. These three opinions are from Ibn ʿAbbas.

The fourth: they loved to be praised for their saying, "We are upon the religion of Ibrahim," and they were not upon it. Said by Saʿid ibn Jubayr.

The fifth: they loved to be praised for their saying, "We are content with what the Prophet has brought," and they were not so. Said by Qatada. These are the opinions of those who said they are the Jews.

The sixth: that they used to swear to the Muslims, when they gained victory, "Indeed we have been gladdened by your victory," and they were not so. Said by Abu Saʿid al-Khudri. This is the view of those who said they are the hypocrites.

The words of the Most High: (So do not think them) — Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read: "fa-la yahsabunnahum," with the ya' (yā') and a damma on the ba' (bā'). Nafi', Ibn ʿAmir, ʿAsim, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read with the ta' (tā') and a fatha on the ba' (bā'). Al-Zajjaj said: "Tahsabannahum" was repeated because of the length of the narrative, and the Arabs repeat "hasibta" and similar forms when the narrative is long, to indicate that what follows is connected to the first, and for emphasis. So you say: "Do not suppose Zayd, when he comes and speaks to you with such-and-such, that you should suppose him truthful."

The words of the Most High: ﴿with a salvation﴾ — Ibn Zayd and Ibn Qutayba said: "with a means of deliverance."

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 189:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ — in it is a refutation of those who say that He is poor.

And in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾ — it is a threat to them; that is, if He willed, He would hasten their punishment.

(p-526) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾. Concerning the occasion of its revelation there are three opinions.

The first: "The Quraysh said to the Jews, 'What did Moses bring you?' They said, 'His staff and his white hand.' And they said to the Christians, 'What did Jesus bring you?' They said, 'He used to heal the blind and the leper, and revive the dead.' So they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, 'Ask your Lord to make Safa gold for us.' Then this verse was revealed." Narrated by Ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: The people of Makkah asked him to bring them a sign, and this verse was revealed. Narrated by Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas.

The third: When the saying of Him, may He be exalted, ﴿And your God is one God﴾ [al-Baqarah: 163] was revealed, the Quraysh said, "He has made our gods equal; bring us a sign," and then this verse was revealed. Said by Abu al-Duha, whose name is Muslim ibn Subayh. As for the interpretation of the verse, it has already passed.

(p-527) His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those who remember Allah standing, sitting, and lying on their sides﴾. Regarding this remembrance there are three opinions.

The first: it is remembrance within the prayer, one prays standing; if he is unable, then sitting; if he is unable, then lying on his side. This is the view of ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Qatādah.

The second: it is remembrance within the prayer and outside it. This is the view of a group of the exegetes (mufassirūn).

The third: it is fear. The meaning is: they fear Allah standing in their conduct, sitting in their ease, and on their sides in their sleep.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾. Ibn Fāris said: tafakkur (reflection) is the heart's turning over of a matter. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Two moderate rakʿahs in reflection are better than a night of standing in prayer while the heart is heedless."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Our Lord﴾. Al-Zajjāj said: its meaning is that they say: ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain﴾, that is, You created it as evidence of You and of the truth of what Your prophets brought. The meaning of ﴿Glory be to You﴾ is: freedom for You from imperfection, and declaring You far above that You would have created them in vain. ﴿So protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾, for we have affirmed that You have a Garden and a Fire.

(p-528) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, indeed You, whoever You admit to the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: In the language, al-mukhza (the one disgraced) is the one humiliated and belittled because of a matter that has befallen him and because of a proof. It is said: akhzaytuhu, meaning: I made him bound by a proof with which I humiliated him.

As for whom this disgrace applies to, there are two opinions.

One: it applies to those who enter it (the Fire) to abide in it forever. This was said by Anas ibn Malik, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, and Muqatil.

The second: it applies to every one who enters it. This meaning is related from Jabir ibn Abdullah, and it was chosen by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari and Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And there are no helpers for the wrongdoers﴾. Ibn Abbas said: And there is no one for the polytheists to prevent them from the punishment of Allah, Exalted is He.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 193:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller (munadiyan)﴾. Regarding the caller there are two opinions.

The first: he is the Prophet ﷺ. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Zayd, and Muqatil.

The second: he is the Qur'an. This was said by Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, and al-Tabari (Ibn Jarir al-Tabari) chose it.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿calling to faith (li-l-iman)﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions.

The first: its meaning is "calling to faith" (yunadi ila al-iman), and similar to it is: ﴿Who guided us to this﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 43], and ﴿because your Lord has inspired it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 5], meaning: guided us to this, and inspired to it. This was said by al-Farra'.

The second: it is inverted in order (muqaddam wa-muakhkhar), and the meaning is: "We heard a caller calling for faith." This was said by Abu ʿUbayda.

(p-529) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And expiate from us our misdeeds (sayyi'atina)﴾. Muqatil said: wipe out our sins from us. Others said: cover them over for us. It has been said: he combined the forgiveness of sins with the expiation of misdeeds, because forgiveness comes by mere bounty, while expiation comes by performing good deeds. ﴿And cause us to die with the righteous (al-abrar)﴾. Nafi', Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read "al-abrar", "al-ashrar", "dhata qarar" and what is similar to them with an intermediate vowel between fath and kasr. Ibn Kathir and ʿAsim read with fath. The meaning of "maʿa al-abrar" is "among them." Ibn ʿAbbas said: they are the prophets and the righteous.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 194:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: they mean Paradise. "Through Your messengers" means: through their tongues.

If it is said: what is the point of this request, since Allah does not break His promise? On this there are three answers.

The first: it came in the form of a request, but its meaning is a statement. Its implied sense is: "So we have believed, so forgive us, that You may give us what You promised us."

The second: it is a request to Him that He make them among those to whom He gives what He promised, not that they deserved it, for had they asserted with certainty that they were among the righteous, that would have been self-praise.

The third: it is a request to hasten what He promised them of victory over the enemies, since He promised them victory not limited to a fixed time, so they desired its hastening. Ibn Jarir mentioned these answers, and said: the most correct of the statements is that this is the description of the emigrants (muhajirun), who desired the hastening of victory over their enemies. It is as though they said: "We have no patience with Your forbearance toward the enemies, so hasten their humiliation and our triumph over them."

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 195:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So their Lord answered them﴾ "It is related from Umm Salamah that she said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I do not hear the mention of women in migration (hijrah) with anything?' So this verse was revealed." Istajaba (answered) means ajaba (answered). The meaning: He answered them by saying to them: "Indeed I do not waste the work of any worker among you, whether male or female."

Regarding the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿some of you are from others﴾ there are three opinions.

The first: some of you are from others in religion, in support, and in allegiance.

The second: the ruling on all of you regarding reward is one, because males are from females and females are from males. The third: all of you are from Adam and Hawwa' (Eve).

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those who emigrated﴾, that is: they left the homelands, the family and the clans. ﴿and were expelled from their homes﴾, meaning: the believers who were expelled from Makkah by the harm of the polytheists, so they emigrated. ﴿and fought﴾ the polytheists ﴿and were killed.﴾ Ibn Kathir and Ibn 'Amir read: "wa-qatalu wa-qutthilu" with the taa' doubled (intensive). Nafi', Abu 'Amr and 'Asim read: "wa-qatalu wa-qutilu" with the taa' light. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read: "wa-qutilu wa-qatalu". Abu 'Ali said: putting "qutilu" first is permissible, because the item joined by waw (and) may be first in meaning while later in wording.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿as a reward from Allah﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: it is an emphatic infinitive (masdar mu'akkad) for what precedes it, because the meaning of "la-udkhilannahum jannat" (I will certainly admit them to gardens) is "la-uthibannahum" (I will certainly reward them).

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 196–197:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Let not the strutting about of those who disbelieve in the land deceive you﴾, the scholars differed concerning whom it was revealed, on two views.

One of them: that it was revealed concerning the Jews. Then, concerning this, there are two statements.

One of them: that the Jews used to travel through the land and acquire wealth, so this verse was revealed. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: "That the Prophet ﷺ wished to borrow barley from some of them, but he refused except against a pledge. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'If he had given it to me, I would have repaid it. Indeed I am trustworthy in the heavens and trustworthy on the earth,' so this was revealed." This was mentioned by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi.

The second view: that it was revealed concerning the polytheists of the Arabs, who were in ease and comfort. Some of the believers said: "Hardship has destroyed us, while the enemies of Allah are as you see." So this verse was revealed. This is the statement of Muqatil. Qatada said: "The address is to the Prophet ﷺ, but what is meant is others." Others said: "He was addressed only for the sake of discipline and warning, even though he would not be deceived."

Concerning the meaning of "their strutting about," there are three statements.

One of them: their dealing in trade. This was said by Ibn Abbas, al-Farra', Ibn Qutayba, and al-Zajjaj.

The second: the turning of their night and day, and the blessings that flow to them. This was said by Ikrima and Muqatil.

The third: their strutting about, not being seized for their sins. This was mentioned by some of the exegetes. Al-Zajjaj said: "That gain and profit is a little enjoyment." Ibn Abbas said: "A small benefit in this world." And al-Mihad: the bedding.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 196–197:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Let not the strutting about of those who disbelieve in the land deceive you﴾, the scholars differed concerning whom it was revealed, on two views.

One of them: that it was revealed concerning the Jews. Then, concerning this, there are two statements.

One of them: that the Jews used to travel through the land and acquire wealth, so this verse was revealed. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: "That the Prophet ﷺ wished to borrow barley from some of them, but he refused except against a pledge. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'If he had given it to me, I would have repaid it. Indeed I am trustworthy in the heavens and trustworthy on the earth,' so this was revealed." This was mentioned by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi.

The second view: that it was revealed concerning the polytheists of the Arabs, who were in ease and comfort. Some of the believers said: "Hardship has destroyed us, while the enemies of Allah are as you see." So this verse was revealed. This is the statement of Muqatil. Qatada said: "The address is to the Prophet ﷺ, but what is meant is others." Others said: "He was addressed only for the sake of discipline and warning, even though he would not be deceived."

Concerning the meaning of "their strutting about," there are three statements.

One of them: their dealing in trade. This was said by Ibn Abbas, al-Farra', Ibn Qutayba, and al-Zajjaj.

The second: the turning of their night and day, and the blessings that flow to them. This was said by Ikrima and Muqatil.

The third: their strutting about, not being seized for their sins. This was mentioned by some of the exegetes. Al-Zajjaj said: "That gain and profit is a little enjoyment." Ibn Abbas said: "A small benefit in this world." And al-Mihad: the bedding.

ُ"Allah's words: ﴿But those who fear their Lord﴾. Abu Ja'far read "lakin" (but) here with the shadda (lakinna), and in (Surat az-Zumar). Muqatil said: they affirmed God's oneness (tawhid). Ibn 'Abbas said: "nuzul" means reward (thawab). Ibn Faris said: "nuzul" is what is prepared for the nazil, and the nazil is the guest."

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 199:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah﴾. The scholars differed concerning whom it was revealed, giving four opinions.

The first: it was revealed concerning an-Najashi (the Negus), because when he died the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed over him. Someone said: "He prays over this Christian foreigner (ʿilj), while he is in his own land?!" So this verse was revealed. This is the statement of Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah, Ibn ʿAbbas, and Anas. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: it was concerning him and his companions.

(p-533). The second: it was revealed concerning the believers among the People of the Scripture, from the Jews and the Christians. Abu Salih narrated this meaning from Ibn ʿAbbas, and Mujahid said likewise.

The third: it was revealed concerning ʿAbdullah ibn Salam and his companions. This was said by Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Zayd, and Muqatil.

The fourth: it was revealed concerning forty people from the people of Najran, thirty from the Abyssinians, and eight from the Romans, who were upon the religion of ʿIsa, and they believed in the Prophet (ﷺ). This was said by ʿAta'.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And what has been revealed to you﴾ means: the Qur'an. ﴿And what has been revealed to them﴾ means: their Scripture.

Al-Khashiʿ (those who humble themselves) means: the humble. ﴿They do not sell the verses of Allah for a small price﴾ means: for a worldly gain, as the leaders of the Jews did. The explanation of the swiftness of the reckoning has already passed.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 3, verse 200:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, be patient﴾. Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman said: It was revealed concerning waiting for prayer after prayer, when there was no military expedition to garrison (yurabitu). Regarding that which they were commanded to be patient in, there are five opinions.

The first: trials and jihad. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: the religion. This was said by al-Hasan, al-Qurazi, and al-Zajjaj.

The third: calamities. This was also narrated from al-Hasan. The fourth: the obligatory duties. This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The fifth: obedience to God. This was said by Qatadah. Regarding that which they were commanded to endure (musabarah) there are two opinions.

One: the enemy. This was said by Ibn Abbas and the majority.

The second: the promise that God made to them. This was said by Ata' and al-Qurazi. Regarding that which they were commanded to garrison (murabatah) for, there are two opinions.

One: fighting the enemies. This was said by Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others. Ibn Qutaybah said: The origin of murabatah and ribat (garrison duty, stationing forces at the frontier) is that these people tie up their horses and those people tie up their horses at the frontier, each one readying himself for his companion.

The second: that it is the prayer, that they were commanded to garrison (keep vigil) for it. This was said by Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman. We have already mentioned in (al-Baqarah) the meaning of "la'alla" (perhaps/so that) and the meaning of "al-falah" (success).

Completed, by the help of God, Blessed and Exalted, is the first part of the book "Zad al-Masir fi 'Ilm al-Tafsir" (Provision of the Journey in the Science of Qur'anic Interpretation). It is followed by the second part, whose beginning is: the tafsir of Surah (al-Nisa').
